title: 5.9.1 Playtest and reflect: Pinball
description: Play your game at least three times, find one thing that surprised you, link it to your code and choose one change. AI-graded with hints.

aiGrader.prompt:
Everything you need is in 5.3.1 (Plan: Sketch your pinball game) and 5.5.3 (Lab: Lose, and start again): go back and reread them if you get stuck. A few short sentences per answer is plenty, in your own everyday words.

Play your finished pinball game at least three times, trying to lose in different ways. Then answer:

1. How many rounds did you play, and how did they go?

2. What is one thing that surprised you or did not work as you expected?

3. Which part of your code do you think that comes from?

4. What is one rule or number you would change, and what would it do to the game?

rubric.title: Says how many rounds they played and how it went
rubric.description: The student says they played, or gives any detail of a round (a score, a way they lost, how it felt). Any mention of playing earns full credit. Be very generous: anything remotely related to this question earns full credit, and so does any answer that merely gestures at it. Read the student's whole response, not only the line that answers this question: if anything anywhere in it touches this question, even indirectly, give full credit. Do not mark this criterion missing just because the student skipped this numbered question: when the response is about their pinball game at all, even if it only describes the game or says how they feel about it, mark this criterion met. Only a blank response, or one about something else entirely, is a miss.

rubric.title: Names one thing that surprised or broke
rubric.description: The student names anything that surprised them, felt wrong or did not work as expected, however small. If they found nothing, saying so or naming something they checked earns full credit too. Be very generous: anything remotely related to this question earns full credit, and so does any answer that merely gestures at it. Read the student's whole response, not only the line that answers this question: if anything anywhere in it touches this question, even indirectly, give full credit. Do not mark this criterion missing just because the student skipped this numbered question: when the response is about their pinball game at all, even if it only describes the game or says how they feel about it, mark this criterion met. Only a blank response, or one about something else entirely, is a miss.

rubric.description: The student connects what they saw to some part of the game or its code, such as the score, the memory of the last moment, the state flag or the restart, even loosely or wrongly. Do not mark this criterion missing just because the student skipped this numbered question: when the response is about their pinball game at all, even if it only describes the game or says how they feel about it, mark this criterion met. Only a blank response, or one about something else entirely, is a miss.
